title: Proper-support Grothendieck existence for algebraic spaces
statement: Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and suppose $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ is an isomorphism. Give $\operatorname{Spec}A$ a specified map to $S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $p:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a separated finite-type morphism of algebraic spaces [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Put $Y_n=Y\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and let $j_n:Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ be the canonical closed immersion. Modules are on the small etale ringed site, with quasi-coherence and tensor pullback as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it is the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules. A finite type quasi-coherent module $F$ on an algebraic space $Y$ has support proper over a scheme $T$ if there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, with $Z\to T$ proper, and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ with $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $\mathcal D$ be the category whose objects are finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules with support proper over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and whose morphisms are all module homomorphisms. Let $\widehat{\mathcal D}$ have objects systems $(F_n,\alpha_n)_{n\geq1}$, where $F_n$ is finitely presented quasi-coherent on $Y_n$, $\alpha_n:j_n^*F_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_n$, and $F_1$ has support proper over $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Morphisms are families of module homomorphisms commuting with the $\alpha_n$. Then the tensor restriction functor $\mathcal D\to\widehat{\mathcal D}$ is an equivalence of categories. No flatness hypothesis on $Y$, on $F$, or on the $F_n$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 08BE (theorem-grothendieck-existence), 08BF (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem); the finite-presentation formulation uses spaces-cohomology.tex, lemma-coherent-Noetherian, and proper support is expressed by its closed-carrier convention.

proof.text: Write $J=I\mathcal O_Y$. The Noetherian-coherent finiteness theorem makes $Y$ and its closed subspaces Noetherian and identifies finite presentation with coherence. The proper-carrier theorem identifies the support condition with properness of the scheme-theoretic support. Apply the closed-adic dictionary termwise: $F_n$ is sent to its pushforward to $Y$, killed by $J^n$, and the adjacent restriction isomorphisms become quotient transition isomorphisms. This identifies the target category with the proper-support subcategory of $\mathrm{Coh}(Y,J)$, on arrows as well as objects, and identifies tensor restriction with completion. Completion lands in this subcategory: if $w:W\hookrightarrow Y$ is a proper closed carrier of $F$, the ideal of $W$ kills $F$ (it acts through $\mathcal O_Y\to w_*\mathcal O_W$), so the closed-adic dictionary writes $F=w_*G$ with $G$ coherent and $F/J^nF\simeq w_*(G/(J\mathcal O_W)^nG)$, which has the same proper carrier $W$. Properness over $A/I$ and over $A$ agrees for a closed subspace factoring through $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$: one direction is proper composition, and the other is the proper cancellation theorem with the separated closed base immersion.

source.place: Tags 08B7, 08B8 and 08BF; translation of support and of the functor.

proof.text: For coherent $F,G$ with proper support, put $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom(F,G)$. The completion-Hom lemma makes $\mathcal H$ coherent. By the carrier theorem choose a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ with $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ proper and $F\simeq i_*F'$; the ideal $K_Z$ of $Z$ acts on $i_*F'$ through $\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$, so $K_ZF=0$. For local sections $a$ of $K_Z$ and $\varphi$ of $\mathcal H$, $(a\varphi)(s)=\varphi(as)=0$, so $K_Z\mathcal H=0$. The closed-adic dictionary ($Z$ is Noetherian) gives a coherent $Q$ on $Z$ with $\mathcal H\simeq i_*Q$ and $i_*(Q/I^nQ)\simeq\mathcal H/J^n\mathcal H$ compatibly with the transitions, and its thickening clause identifies $Q/I^nQ$ with the tensor restriction of $Q$ to $Z\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$. Sections of a direct image over $Y$ are sections over the whole source, so quotient global sections on $Y$ equal those on $Z$. Proper coherent higher images and affine-chart calculus make $\Gamma(Z,Q)$ a finite $A$-module: it is the sections of the coherent zeroth direct image on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. It is complete by finite-module completeness over a complete Noetherian ring. Formal functions at degree zero therefore identifies $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H)$ with $\varprojlim_n\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H/J^n\mathcal H)$. Composing with completion-Hom gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(F,G)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\widehat F_J,\widehat G_J)$; the compatibility clause says this is the actual completion map. This proves full faithfulness for every separated finite-type $Y$ over $A$, before any existence argument.

source.place: Tag 08BE first paragraph, expanding Tag 08B9 via 08B6 and formal functions.

proof.text: It remains to prove essential surjectivity. For a quasi-coherent ideal $L\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$, let $P(L)$ say every proper-support $J$-system annihilated termwise by $L$ is algebraizable with proper support. The empty space and the zero system are immediate. If $P(0)$ fails, the ascending chain condition gives a maximal ideal $L$ for which $P(L)$ fails. By the closed-adic dictionary replace $Y$ by $V(L)$; its coherent modules and systems are precisely those killed by $L$ on the old space, and proper support is preserved. Every nonzero quasi-coherent ideal of this quotient corresponds to an ideal $L'\supsetneq L$, so $P(L')$ holds by maximality. The algebraization it gives lies on $V(L')$: let $M'$ be killed by $L'$ and $F$ coherent with proper support with $\widehat F_J\simeq M'$. Then $L'(F/J^nF)=0$, so $L'F\subseteq J^nF$ for all $n$. The quotient $\pi:F\to F'=F/L'F$ is killed by the ideal of a proper carrier of $F$, so it has that carrier by the closed-adic dictionary, and $F'/J^nF'=F/(L'F+J^nF)=F/J^nF$; thus $\widehat\pi$ is the identity on each level. Step 2 gives $\sigma:F'\to F$ with $\widehat\sigma=\widehat\pi^{-1}$, and injectivity of the step-2 bijection gives $\sigma\pi=1$ and $\pi\sigma=1$. Hence $L'F=0$, and the closed-adic dictionary puts $F$ and the isomorphism on $V(L')$. Full faithfulness on this quotient and on all its closed subspaces is already step 2. Fix a proper-support system $M$ on this quotient; algebraizing it will contradict the choice of $L$.

source.place: Tag 08BE, maximal bad ideal and replacement by its closed subspace.

proof.text: For this nonempty quotient $Y$, the dense-open Chow modification supplies $q:V\to Y$, with $V$ a Noetherian scheme immersed over $A$ into finite projective space, and $q$ an isomorphism over a dense open $U$. The tensor pullback system $q^*M$ is a coherent $I\mathcal O_V$-system because tensor pullback of a finite presentation remains a finite presentation: it preserves the finite free terms and their cokernel; quotient transitions are preserved by associativity of tensor product. Its first term has support proper over $A$. Let $c:C\hookrightarrow Y$ be a proper closed carrier of $M_1$ with ideal $K_C$, so $K_CM_1=0$. Let $V_C=V\times_YC\hookrightarrow V$ be the base-changed closed immersion. Its ideal is $K_C\mathcal O_V$: on etale charts, the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(R/K)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ along $R\to B$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)$. Sections of $q^{-1}K_C$ act by zero on $q^{-1}M_1$, so $K_C\mathcal O_V$ kills $q^*M_1$. Base change makes $V_C\to C$ proper, and proper composition makes $V_C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ proper. After the Zariski--etale passage below, the scheme proper-support criterion (a closed subscheme proper over $A$ whose ideal kills the module) shows that $\operatorname{Supp}(q^*M_1)$ is proper over $A$. By the support-pullback formula this support is $|q|^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}M_1)$. Use the scheme Zariski--etale equivalence termwise, including its natural tensor-pullback comparison, to regard $q^*M$ as a Zariski coherent formal system on the actual scheme $V$. Apply new-chow-algebraization-core with its scheme $Z=V$, its proper map the identity of $V$, and the immersion just obtained. It gives a coherent $E$ on $V$ with proper support over $A$ and a compatible isomorphism $\beta:q^*M\simeq\widehat E$. Bring $E$ and $\beta$ back through the same scheme-site equivalence. No assertion that $Y$ is a scheme is used.

source.place: Tag 08BE, Chow and projective algebraization paragraphs, reusing the existing scheme compactification/algebraization input.

proof.text: Let $K$ cut out the reduced closed complement $Y\setminus U$; existence of this closed subspace and its quasi-coherent ideal is the closed-support convention. Its restriction to $U$ is the unit ideal. Since $U$ is dense in nonempty $Y$, it is nonempty, so $K^e\ne0$ for every $e\geq1$ (its stalk on $U$ is the unit ideal). Step 3 therefore algebraizes every proper-support system killed by $K^e$ by a coherent module killed by $K^e$. The closed-adic dictionary and step 2 upgrade this to an equivalence for completion on every $V(K^e)$: essential surjectivity is step 3 and full faithfulness is step 2.

source.place: Tag 08BE, final paragraph: the exceptional ideal and the induction hypothesis on its powers.

proof.text: Set $H=q_*E$. Proper coherent higher images makes $H$ coherent. To check its proper support rather than assume it: through the scheme-site equivalence, $E$ is a coherent Zariski module on the scheme $V$ with support proper over $A$. The scheme proper-support criterion gives a closed subscheme $c_E:C_E\hookrightarrow V$, proper over $A$, whose ideal $K_E$ kills $E$. Apply the proper schematic-image theorem to $q\circ c_E:C_E\to Y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The target morphism is separated and locally of finite type, so $qc_E$ factors through a closed subspace $z:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ proper over $A$. Let $K_Z$ be the ideal of $Z$. The factorization means $q^\sharp(K_Z)\subseteq K_E$. By the defining chart-limit description of $q_*$, a local section $a$ of $K_Z$ acts on each chart value $E(T)$ through $q^\sharp(a)$, hence by zero: $K_ZH=0$. The closed-adic dictionary writes $H\simeq z_*Q$ with $Q$ coherent on $Z$. Thus $Z$ is a proper closed carrier of $H$, and $H$ has proper support over $A$.

source.place: Tag 08BE, last paragraph: coherence and proper support of the comparison target.

proof.text: The modification comparison applied to $q$, $J$, $K$, $M$, $E$ and $\beta$ gives $a:M\to\widehat H_J$ with uniformly $K$-power-annihilated component kernels and cokernels. Its hypotheses hold: $q$ is representable proper, both spaces are Noetherian, and $q$ is an isomorphism over $Y\setminus V(K)=U$. Step 6 gives proper support of $H$; step 5 gives the completion equivalence on every $V(K^e)$. These are exactly the hypotheses of bounded-exceptional-torsion devissage. It yields a coherent $F$ with proper support and $\widehat F_J\simeq M$, contradicting the chosen maximal failure. Consequently there is no bad ideal and every proper-support system on the original $Y$ is algebraizable.

source.place: Tag 08BE, final application of Tags 08BD and 08BC.

proof.text: Full faithfulness from step 2 and essential surjectivity from step 7 give the required equivalence: choose an algebraization and a compatible isomorphism for each system; lift each morphism uniquely by the Hom bijection. Injectivity of that bijection proves the identity and composition laws and the naturality of the chosen isomorphisms. The closed-adic dictionary of step 1 identifies these isomorphisms with all the specified adjacent tensor restrictions. No step assumed flatness of the spaces or modules.
